high: Gate C/D failure: the player can blindly add any two optional acts and submit successfully. Every two-act lineup fits comfortably, so neither the changeover document nor meaningful scheduling judgment is required on the first playthrough.

Answer-leaking retry hint: the first overtime submission immediately states the core solution—reduce acts or place same-setup acts consecutively—and points directly to the changeover document, contrary to the required staged-hint approach.
medium: Act cards display only name and runtime, not their band/light/none setup type. The rule explains setup categories, but the player cannot directly inspect the category assigned to each act and must infer it from names or observed transition values.

The new QA harness validates schedule arithmetic but does not test the exploitable minimum-content success path or the component's pinning behavior; its final two checks verify only must=true metadata.

The mission says the current program cannot finish on time, yet gameplay starts with only opening and ending. A player who adds two acts never encounters the stated overcrowded schedule or the repaired trade-off.
low: Pinned-boundary controls appear enabled even though move() rejects them: opening's down button, ending's up button, and adjacent optional-act buttons toward a pinned slot can be clicked with no effect.

recommended_actions: Require a genuinely constrained lineup before success—for example, require exactly four optional acts or initialize all five acts—so first-play completion necessarily involves choosing a cut and, for at least some cuts, ordering judgment.
Show a neutral setup-type label or icon on every act card without visually privileging any answer.
On the first overtime attempt, show only the changed schedule/overrun consequence; defer the explicit same-setup grouping hint until a later failed attempt.
Extend the harness with component-level checks for blind two-act submission, over-time rejection, open/end pinning, enabled-button behavior, and setup-type visibility.
Disable every move button whose requested destination is a pinned slot, or omit controls from the mandatory opening/ending rows.
